### Read the Bible: Deuteronomy 8
Author: D. A. Carson
Site: The Gospel Coalition
URL: https://www.thegospelcoalition.org/devotionals/read-the-bible/deut-8-psalm-91-isaiah-36-revelation-6/
Passage: Deuteronomy 8:1-20
Points:
- God sovereignly guided the wilderness journey to test and humble His people through loving fatherly discipline.
- The experience of physical hunger and supernatural manna proved that genuine life depends on God's words.
- Fallen human nature easily fixates on good gifts while ignoring the Giver who provided them.
- Material prosperity introduces the dangerous temptation toward pride and taking personal credit for wealth.
- Believers must actively treasure God's word above earthly abundance and acknowledge Him as their provider.

### Why Remember?
Author: J. Reid
Site: Ligonier Ministries
URL: https://learn.ligonier.org/articles/why-remember
Passage: Deuteronomy 8:1-20
Points:
- Remembering God's past works is grounded in His unchanging character and covenant promises.
- The wilderness hardships and daily manna taught Israel to trust God for their basic necessities rather than human effort alone.
- Physical deprivation functioned as a divine classroom to expose the heart and foster filial obedience.
- Seasons of comfort and prosperity pose a great spiritual risk of self-sufficiency and idolatry.
- Recalling God’s past faithfulness equips believers to persevere through trials and remain humble during times of success.

### Bible Pathway - Mar. 4, 2010
Author: Bible Pathway Ministries
Site: Crosswalk
URL: https://www.crosswalk.com/devotionals/biblepathways/bible-pathway-mar-4-2010-11627055.html
Passage: Deuteronomy 8:3
Points:
- God allowed Israel to hunger before feeding them with manna to teach ultimate dependence on His word.
- Jesus used this passage as His primary defense against Satan's temptation to pursue physical gratification independently of God.
- Daily reading and hiding God's Word in our hearts equips the Holy Spirit to bring truth to mind during spiritual attacks.
- Believers must heed Moses' warning against self-reliance, recognizing that God alone grants the ability to produce wealth.
- Keeping God's commandments with a humble and grateful heart is essential for walking in His blessing.
